title: Formal Verification Database — Overview and definition
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Proof techniques, invariants, specifications, and verified implementation examples. The Formal Verification Database is where software stops being 'probably right' and becomes proven right: specifications written in precise logic, invariants that must hold at every step, proof techniques that discharge them, and implementation examples that passed verification. Testing can only show the presence of bugs; verification proves their absence for the specified properties. Each record pairs a specification with its proof — and is honest about what was NOT proven.

title: Formal Verification Database — Knowledge: technical reference
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Foundations. Hoare triple {P} C {Q}: if P holds before command C, Q holds after. Loop rule needs invariant I: {I and B} body {I}, then {I} while B do body {I and not B}. Induction: prove P(0), prove P(n)->P(n+1). Model checking: exhaustively explore finite state spaces; specify in temporal logic (AG p = p always holds). SMT: satisfiability modulo theories — feed constraints to a solver, unsatisfiable means the property holds. Invariant patterns: loop bounds, data-structure shape (e.g. 'list is sorted'), resource accounting. Proof workflow: write spec -> propose invariants -> discharge with solver/interactive proof -> record assumptions. Honesty rule: the scope statement is part of the record; 'verified' without a scope statement is not a verification.

demo.title: Execution: build pipeline generate-build-test-fix
demo.code: let attempts=0;function build(code){attempts++;return code.includes('BUG')?{ok:false,log:'compile error: BUG token'}:{ok:true,log:'build clean'};}let code='v1 with BUG';let res=build(code);while(!res.ok&&attempts<5){code=code.replace('BUG','FIX');res=build(code);}J({attempts,ok:res.ok,log:res.log});assert(res.ok&&attempts===2,'buildloop');

demo.title: Verification: property-based test of sort
demo.code: function prop(a){const s=[...a].sort((x,y)=>x-y);const sorted=s.every((v,i)=>i===0||s[i-1]<=v);const perm=JSON.stringify([...a].sort((x,y)=>x-y))===JSON.stringify(s);return sorted&&perm;}let seed=42;function rnd(){seed=(seed*1103515245+12345)&0x7fffffff;return seed%100;}let pass=true;for(let t=0;t<200;t++){const a=Array.from({length:10},rnd);if(!prop(a)){pass=false;break;}}J({trials:200,pass});assert(pass,'property');

title: Formal Verification Database — Verification: tests and limitations
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Tests: Hoare test (valid triples pass, invalid fail); invariant test (preserved invariants pass, broken ones fail with counterexample state); scope test (records without assumptions are rejected); determinism test. Limitations: demos use symbolic execution on small states, not full provers; real verification needs interactive proof assistants or SMT solvers; assumption lists need expert review. Every record states its proof status: proven, partially-proven, or outline-only.

demo.title: Execution: debugging signature match and bisection
demo.code: const sigs=[{re:/index out of range/i,cause:'off-by-one'},{re:/null|undefined/i,cause:'null-deref'}];const err='IndexError: list index out of range';const m=sigs.find(s=>s.re.test(err));const commits=['c1','c2','c3','c4','c5','c6','c7','c8'];const bad=5;let lo=0,hi=commits.length-1,steps=0;while(lo<hi){steps++;const mid=(lo+hi)>>1;if(mid>=bad)hi=mid;else lo=mid+1;}J({cause:m.cause,culprit:commits[lo],steps});assert(m.cause==='off-by-one'&&commits[lo]==='c6'&&steps===3,'debug');
